THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)

THE SESSION'S EARLIER GUESSES AND HYPOTHESES:
  [Y1] guess: lc is saturated at the link layer; payload goodputs omit packet headers, so their sum can be below 100 Mbps.
  [Y2] guess: fb sends 80 Mbps but receives only its normalized scheduler part 0.5/(0.5+0.5)=0.5, about 50 Mbps, so the excess fills the 100-packet queue and drops.
  [Y3] guess: fa_goodput_bps tracks the normalized scheduler part p/(p+0.5) when TCP has enough data to fill that part.
  [Y4] guess: The 100-packet queue is too small for UDP arrivals, causing fb drops even when the scheduler part would allow enough service.
  [Y5] guess: fa_goodput_bps is mainly limited by TCP congestion-control dynamics and queue drops, not by the scheduler part, so changing lc.queue.parts.fa over this range will not more than double it.
  [Y6] guess: The scheduler is work-conserving: when fb has no packet waiting, fa receives the unused lc capacity.
  [Y7] guess: fb_loss_frac is the offered-service shortfall, 1 - fb_goodput_bps/80000000, when fb's weighted service is below its 80 Mbps offer; queue length only buffers transients.
  [Y8] guess: lc_util counts link-layer bits including headers, so payload sum can be below 100 Mbps; fb's queue stays full and tail-drops because fb is offered more than its weighted service.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: 1 %: in a decision rule == holds for two values closer than that; <, <=, > and >= compare the numbers as measured, and a check that two measured results decide by less is marked.

shown:
THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: 1 %: in a decision rule == holds for two values closer than that; <, <=, > and >= compare the numbers as measured, and a check that two measured results decide by less is marked.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)

Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: 1 %: in a decision rule == holds for two values closer than that; <, <=, > and >= compare the numbers as measured, and a check that two measured results decide by less is marked.

THE RESULT the guess is about: At p=0.185, length=1000 lowers fb_loss_frac by 0.006832 and lc_drops_fb by 245 while fb_goodput_bps is unchanged and lc_q_fb grows by about 167 packets.
THE GUESS of why it came out so: fb_loss_frac is drops over packets sent in the measured window, while fb_goodput_bps counts only delivered packets; a larger queue leaves more packets queued at the end, so fewer drops are offset by more undelivered backlog, leaving delivered goodput unchanged.
THE HYPOTHESIS H4: At lc.queue.parts.fa=0.186, increasing lc.queue.length from 100 to 1000 leaves fb_goodput_bps within 1%, makes fb_loss_frac lower than the offered-service shortfall by more than 0.005, and increases lc_q_fb by more than 100 packets during the measured window.
DECISION RULE: fb_goodput_bps@p0186_L1000 == fb_goodput_bps@p0186_L100 AND fb_loss_frac@p0186_L1000 < (1 - fb_goodput_bps@p0186_L1000 / 80000000) - 0.005 AND q_fb_last@p0186_L1000 - q_fb_first@p0186_L1000 > 100
THE GUESS THIS RULE COMPETES WITH [Y7]: the result it explains: p015 r004 has fb_goodput_bps=75311040 and fb_loss_frac=0.058576, while p005 r002 has fb_goodput_bps=79999360 and fb_loss_frac=0.0. | its guess: fb_loss_frac is the offered-service shortfall, 1 - fb_goodput_bps/80000000, when fb's weighted service is below its 80 Mbps offer; queue length only buffers transients.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: 1 %: in a decision rule == holds for two values closer than that; <, <=, > and >= compare the numbers as measured, and a check that two measured results decide by less is marked.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: 1 %: in a decision rule == holds for two values closer than that; <, <=, > and >= compare the numbers as measured, and a check that two measured results decide by less is marked.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: 1 %: in a decision rule == holds for two values closer than that; <, <=, > and >= compare the numbers as measured, and a check that two measured results decide by less is marked.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: 1 %: in a decision rule == holds for two values closer than that; <, <=, > and >= compare the numbers as measured, and a check that two measured results decide by less is marked.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: lc.queue.parts.fa (0.05 to 4, default 0.5); lc.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); fa.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, default TcpCubic)

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of four hosts: a, b, r and c. Host a sends a TCP flow, fa, to c; host b sends a UDP flow, fb, to c at a constant rate (80Mbps, packets of 1400 bytes). Both reach c through r, which forwards them. Link la joins a and r and link lb joins b and r; each carries 1Gbps. Link lc joins r and c and carries only 100Mbps with a one-way delay of 1ms: everything the two flows send to c must pass it. On r's side of lc a scheduler divides the link between the two flows by two parts, the knob lc.queue.parts.fa for fa and 0.5 for fb (the parts are divided by their sum); each flow waits in a queue of its own of the knob lc.queue.length packets, and a packet that arrives at a full queue is dropped. How the scheduler behaves when one flow has less to send than its part allows is not described here; finding that out is part of the work. The congestion control of fa is the knob fa.type. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
